title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Are longer films rated more highly? Figure 1 plots each film’s runtime against its IMDb rating.

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
ax.set_xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
ax.set_ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime in minutes against IMDb rating





Mean IMDb rating by decade:

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10
films.groupby("decade")["imdb_rating"].mean().round(2)

decade
1980    8.01
1990    7.70
2000    7.94
2010    7.83
2020    7.44
Name: imdb_rating, dtype: float64

title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Do bigger budgets bring bigger box-office returns? Figure 1 plots each film’s production budget against its worldwide revenue, both in millions of US dollars.

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
ax.set_xlabel("Budget (millions of US dollars)")
ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Production budget against worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

The dataset includes James Bond films from 1995 to 2021. Figure 1 shows their worldwide revenue over time.

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of the James Bond films (millions of US dollars)

title: Box Office Numbers
text:
This site explores films.csv, a dataset of 104 well-known films released between 1980 and 2025. For each film it records the franchise, the approximate production budget and worldwide revenue in millions of US dollars, the runtime in minutes, and the IMDb rating. The figures are rounded and not adjusted for inflation.
